style.value: Restrained editorial motion built from one repeated mechanic: a 1.109s ease-out reveal. Headings rise from a clipped edge, photographs fade, the hero photograph settles from scale 1.1, links underline and project images scale on hover, and a 4px bar tracks scroll progress.

personality.value: Quiet, precise and slow. The same 1.109s timing recurs across unrelated elements, so the page reads as one system rather than a set of independent effects. Nothing moves while the page is idle.

principles.value: Movement is permitted at three moments only: page entry, an element entering the viewport, and direct interaction. There is no looping, ambient, idle or scroll-scrubbed motion.
Reveals animate transform or opacity only; no filter, width, height, background or layout property is animated.
The reference reuses one timing function rather than tuning each element; the demo keeps the shared curve and duration instead of inventing per-element speed.
Every scroll reveal fires once and is unobserved immediately, so re-entering the viewport never replays it.

context.value: Single-page editorial architecture studio portfolio with infrequent navigation and project browsing, so slow reveals and restrained interaction motion are appropriate.
context.note: Inferred from page type and interaction frequency, not a source declaration.

target.value: Section headings, the pull quote and the footer wordmark, plus the hero title; each heading's content is wrapped in a clipped .rise span at runtime

delay.note: The reference gates playback behind its preloader; the demo has none, so the reveal starts immediately.

easing.note: GSAP default power1.out, approximated with easeOutQuad.

notes.value: Reference: splittext lines animate yPercent 101 to 0 with duration Si() = 1.109s and stagger Si(1) = 0.1s, attached to a ScrollTrigger.
The demo lifts one block per heading, so the reference's 0.1s per-line stagger is not reproduced; splitting lines would require runtime line-box measurement.
Section headings fire once when their top crosses 94% of the viewport; the hero title fires once on load.

sourceSupported.value: Heading reveal: yPercent 101 to 0, duration Si() = 1.109s, stagger Si(1) = 0.1s, on a ScrollTrigger, with GSAP's default power1.out ease.
The reference's step function Si(step, offset, base = 0.1) = 0.1 x 1.61803398875^(step - 1) returns 1.109s at the default step and 0.1s at step 1.
Hero image: scale 1.1 to 1 over 2.4s, played when the preloader finishes.
Project images declare transform 1.109s and opacity 0.3s with cubic-bezier(0.17, 0.84, 0.44, 1).
A fixed 4px progress bar (.yap) scales on the X axis from a left origin.
Link underlines scale the X axis with a right-to-left origin flip over 1.109s; project images scale to 1.035 on hover with the same curve.
The reference ships GSAP, ScrollTrigger, SplitText, Lenis and a Three.js/WebGL pipeline; only the behaviours that can be expressed faithfully in CSS and one small script were carried over.

functionalAdditions.value: Keyboard focus parity for link underlines, with a visible 2px accent outline.
Keyboard focus parity for the project image scale, with a card outline.
80ms pressed opacity feedback on links and project cards.
160ms opacity and translateY enter for the demo's own details/summary mobile menu.
Reduced-motion alternative: a static caption underline replaces the project image scale.
A dependency-free IntersectionObserver replaces ScrollTrigger; each target is unobserved after its single reveal.
The scroll bar is throttled to at most one requestAnimationFrame per scroll frame and listens passively.
Heading wrappers are created only when motion.js runs, so without JavaScript every heading is already in its final position.

intentionallyOmitted.value: Lenis smooth scrolling and scroll inertia (html.lenis); the reference also feeds scroll velocity into its WebGL layers.
intentionallyOmitted.note: Intercepting native scrolling would change input feel and accessibility behaviour; the demo keeps native scrolling.

intentionallyOmitted.value: Three.js/WebGL image effects: KTX2 textures, shader hover (uHover 0 to 1, 0.3s power2.out), scroll-scrubbed uniforms and a fixed WebGL canvas.
intentionallyOmitted.note: Requires a WebGL pipeline, the reference's texture assets and a persistent canvas; the demo keeps CSS hover only.

intentionallyOmitted.value: Preloader and its gate on entrance playback (app:preloaderdone hooks).
intentionallyOmitted.note: The demo has no preloader, so entrances start immediately; no artificial loading delay was added.

intentionallyOmitted.value: Nuxt page transitions (.dyh overlay with opacity and clip-path, 0.3s), the custom cursor and the fixed mix-blend header (0.6s).
intentionallyOmitted.note: The demo is a single page with no router, no custom pointer and an absolute header over the hero, so these have no equivalent state to transition.

intentionallyOmitted.value: Marquee text (.oty), the drag gallery (.eun) and scroll-pinned or scrubbed sections.
intentionallyOmitted.note: No marquee, gallery or pinned section exists in the adapted composition; pinned scroll would also trap content on short viewports.

intentionallyOmitted.value: Per-line SplitText staggering, per-word and per-character variants.
intentionallyOmitted.note: Splitting text into measured lines needs runtime line-box measurement; the demo lifts one clipped block per heading and records the missing stagger.

navigation.value: Desktop navigation is replaced by the details/summary menu; underlines and a 160ms panel enter replace desktop hover behaviour.

projectImage.value: The image scale is gated by (hover: hover), so touch layouts use pressed opacity rather than sticky hover scaling.

reveals.value: Heading, image and hero motion are unchanged at 390px; verified with no horizontal overflow (scrollWidth 390).

strategy.value: Disable every CSS transition and animation, remove the hero and heading animations instead of shortening them, resolve all reveal masks to their final state, force scroll-behavior to auto, and keep the scroll bar as an instantly updated position indicator.

alternatives.value: Headings, photographs and the hero render in their final state; no clipped or transparent content remains.
Link and project hover states still change instantly, and the caption gains a 3px-offset underline, so affordance survives.
The scroll bar still communicates position without animating.

risks.value: The reference's 1.109s duration is long for utility feedback; it is retained only for hover, focus and entrance reveals and never blocks navigation or activation.
Large photographs are transformed on hover; overflow: hidden contains the growth and no layout properties animate.
motion.js adds one passive scroll listener, one resize listener and one IntersectionObserver; all are idle between reveals and no animation frame loop runs.
Touch layouts skip hover scaling, avoiding sticky zoom and unnecessary GPU work.

notes.value: No animation library, framework or large dependency was added; motion.js is a single dependency-free file.
Frame timing was probed with CDP rather than filmed: both entrance animations end at identity and every reveal reaches opacity 1 with a none transform.

unresolved: The licensed display typeface and its variable axes cannot be identified from captures; the demo uses a local serif stack.
The reference's statistics and client-wall regions were deliberately excluded because reproducing them would require invented metrics and client identities.

Hover and focus motion was read from live computed styles and confirmed against the production bundle; no screen recording was made, so playback is measured from declared and computed values, not captured frames.

The reference's Lenis inertia, WebGL shader effects, preloader, page-transition overlay, custom cursor, marquee, drag gallery and scroll-pinned sections were observed but intentionally omitted from the adapted composition; each omission is recorded in the motion section.
Reference photography is not licensed for reuse; the demo substitutes Unsplash photographs and records the new composition in the implementation spec.
